answer: Each identity props one canyon bay and files timber props, counted and spaced, locking 75. First fee is 36; the k-th bay costs 36+8(k-1), as each bay is surveyed and load-checked and cannot be reused. The 1000th costs 8028; 1000 clones pay 4,032,000 and lock 75,000. An auditor checks the quill-signed log and recomputes spacing from roof span and rock load tables; spacing too wide, or a registered bay, burns the bond. A rented-prop ring fails: claiming the same bay and props for many identities reuses a listed bay, so later filings burn. An honest miner pays 36 once and recovers its bond.
